record.paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
record.original_question: For integrable equations on a half-line, resolve the mismatch between the well-posed initial-boundary data and the additional dependent boundary quantities required by the Fokas method. In particular, for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on x≥0,t≥0 with smooth compactly supported initial data u(x,0)=u_0(x) and periodic boundary forcing u(0,t)=sin(ω t) with ω≠0, determine the long-time behavior of the solution and decide whether a fully explicit description is possible for general data.

evidence.quote: This is true even in simple cases, such as the following: suppose u(x, t) solves NLS in (x ≥ 0, t ≥ 0) with u(0, t) = sin(ωt), ω ≠ 0, and u(x, 0) = u0(x), where u0 is smooth with compact support. How does u(x, t) behave as t → ∞?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on the quarter plane,
    i u_t + u_{xx} + 2|u|^2 u = 0,    x ≥ 0,  t ≥ 0,
(with either focusing or defocusing sign fixed) supplemented by:
  • initial data u(x,0) = u_0(x), where u_0 is smooth and compactly supported on [0,∞);
  • Dirichlet boundary forcing u(0,t) = sin(ω t), with a fixed real frequency ω ≠ 0.

The Fokas unified transform method represents the solution through a Riemann–Hilbert problem whose data require knowledge of additional boundary values (e.g. u_x(0,t)) beyond the initial-boundary data above. The "Dirichlet-to-Neumann" map needed to recover these unknown boundary quantities from the well-posed data is in general not explicit.

Problem. Determine the long-time asymptotic behavior of u(x,t) as t → ∞, for (x,t) in the quarter plane (in all relevant asymptotic sectors, e.g. x/t fixed). In particular:
  (a) Describe u(x,t) in the limit t → ∞ for general smooth compactly supported initial data u_0.
  (b) Decide whether a fully explicit description of this long-time behavior (including the asymptotics of the unknown Neumann boundary value u_x(0,t)) can be obtained for arbitrary such u_0.
artifact.category_tag: Integrable boundary value problems / Fokas method
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Boutet de Monvel, Its, and Kotlyarov, and later Lenells–Fokas, treated the focusing NLS on the half-line with t-periodic Dirichlet data of the form a·exp(2iωt). They computed the long-time asymptotics via nonlinear steepest descent for the associated Riemann–Hilbert problem and obtained perturbative explicit formulas for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map (asymptotically periodic Neumann values) in special regimes. A complete, fully explicit description for general smooth compactly supported initial data with sin(ωt) boundary forcing does not appear to be available; the underlying Dirichlet-to-Neumann problem is known to be nonlinear and, in some regimes, unstable. The problem is thus partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The Focusing NLS Equation on the Half-Line with Periodic Boundary Conditions: Instability of the Dirichlet to Neumann Map
status_evidence.snippet: Studies focusing NLS on the half-line with periodic Dirichlet data and shows instability of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map.
status_evidence.claim: The Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for periodic boundary data is generally nonlinear and can be unstable, indicating no straightforward explicit description.

status_evidence.title: The Unified Method: II NLS on the Half-Line with t-Periodic Boundary Conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Lenells–Fokas analyze NLS on the half-line with t-periodic boundary data, computing the unknown boundary values asymptotically.
status_evidence.claim: For t-periodic Dirichlet data the Neumann values can be computed perturbatively and are asymptotically periodic, providing partial explicit results.

status_evidence.title: Long-time asymptotics for the focusing NLS equation with time-periodic boundary condition
status_evidence.snippet: Boutet de Monvel–Its–Kotlyarov derive long-time asymptotics in different sectors of the quarter plane for periodic boundary data.
status_evidence.claim: Long-time asymptotics in various sectors have been derived for special periodic boundary data, but not in full generality for arbitrary compactly supported initial data.
